findings.title: Money requested before any viewing
findings.detail: The agent asks for money before you have seen the property in person. Paying before a viewing is the most common way students lose a deposit.

findings.title: In-person viewing refused
findings.detail: The agent will not let you, or someone you trust, see the property in person before you commit. The agent will not let you see the flat unless you pay first, so a real in-person viewing is being withheld.

findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap calculation holds on the quoted figures. Rent is GBP 1300 per calendar month, so annual rent is GBP 15,600. Five weeks is 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500, and the stated deposit is GBP 1,500, so it is at the cap and not above it. Nothing in the contract contradicts this or shows the deposit covers a different tenancy or share. The amount is compliant only if the rule's scope applies. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown in the context, and the rule covers only covered tenancies. The contract does not confirm that the property is in England, that this is an ordinary private tenancy, or that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. This is therefore a correctly limited amount-cap pass, kept conditional on scope. It says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. No substantive counter-evidence defeats the issue, so it is not dismissed. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

findings.title: Credibility you cannot check
findings.detail: This promises safety without saying who guarantees what or how you could check it or claim on it. Calling it a policy makes the demand sound fixed and official; the plain version is that they are refusing a viewing until you pay.

evidence.quote: Our policy remains payment first, viewing afterwards.

findings.title: Wording that hides a plain meaning
findings.detail: This presents a payment demand as if it were for your benefit; the plain version is that they want £1500 before you see the flat.

findings.title: Praise that lowers your guard
findings.detail: This asks you to trust them because they say they are caring; the plain version is that they have not shown you anything you can check. This warm wording softens a refusal of your request; the plain version is that they have not agreed to a viewing first.

findings.title: What the messages actually state
findings.detail: • The student has not viewed Flat 2, 14 Example Mews, London W12 8QT. • The student is asking for a viewing before paying. • A transfer of GBP 1500 is requested to reserve the viewing. • Access to the flat will not be arranged until the transfer arrives in the named account. • The student wants to see the flat before paying. • The agent's stated policy is payment first, viewing afterwards.

findings.title: Rent above the area average
findings.detail: £1,300 a month against roughly £950 for a room in W12 (approximate area figure): about 37% higher. Not a scam sign, but worth knowing.

decision.summary: 3 of 8 checks are suspicious, including payment safety, in person viewing, no pressure. This looks like a likely scam. Do not send money or personal documents.
